title: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)

sections.label: Block budget growth reduction
sections.summary: The Finance Minister announced that Ministries' block budget growth will be reduced from 0.4 to 0.3 times GDP next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Finance Minister announced that growth of Ministries' block budgets will be reduced from 0.4 times of gross domestic product (GDP) to 0.3 times next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Last year, he also announced a permanent 2% downward adjustment to Budget caps and that the agencies are on the lookout for ways to be efficient and effective.

sections.label: School wall replaced with air-conditioning
sections.summary: The principal and contractor agreed not to build a wall, using the savings to air-condition classrooms at no extra cost to MOE or the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Thanks to the good wisdom of the principal and the contractor, they agreed on not building the wall.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Instead, the contractor will use the money saved to install air-conditioning for all the classrooms adjacent to the construction site and the school can get to keep the air-condition machines even after the completion of the projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To top it off, all these improvements to the school environment comes at no additional cost to MOE or the Government.

sections.label: Budget 2018 government spending
sections.summary: Budget 2018 Government spending is estimated at $80 billion, an 8.3% year-on-year increase, mainly for transport, trade and industry and home security.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: For Budget 2018, total spending by the Government is estimated to be $80 billion, representing an increase of 8.3% year-on-year, mainly on the back of increased spending in transport, trade and industry and home security.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Even though Government spending at 19% of GDP is considered lean when compared to other developed countries, the expenditure growth has been on the rise and cost management discipline is more important now than ever.

sections.label: Monitoring spending value-for-money mechanisms
sections.summary: The Member asked the Minister what mechanisms evaluate and monitor spending to ensure value-for-money and accountability on outcomes and spending.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, with significant infrastructure spending and Government programmes yet to come, I would like to ask the Minister what mechanisms are in place to evaluate and monitor spending to ensure value-for-money and accountability on outcomes and spending.

sections.label: Statutory Board Chiefs cooperation duty
sections.summary: Under the new Bill, Chief Executives of Statutory Boards are obliged by law to cooperate and collaborate with other public sector agencies to deliver value to the public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With the new Bill in place, Chief Executives of Statutory Boards will be obliged by law to cooperate and collaborate with other public sector agencies to deliver value to the public.

sections.label: Temasek anti-corruption roundtable
sections.summary: Temasek has taken steps to tackle corruption in its portfolio companies, with Chairman Lim Boon Heng announcing a roundtable in the next few months on governance and ethics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, it was reported yesterday that Temasek has now taken some steps in tackling corruption within its portfolio companies with Chairman Lim Boon Heng announcing a roundtable "in the next few months" focusing on questions of governance and ethics.

sections.label: Temasek and GIC non-interference
sections.summary: A Member asks whether Temasek and GIC share ideas and experience with investee companies to enhance long-term shareholder value, citing Indranee Rajah's statement that Temasek does not interfere in portfolio companies' business decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, during the debate on bribery probe at Keppel Offshore and Marine, Senior Minister of State Indranee Rajah said "likewise, Temasek does not interfere in the business decisions or operations of its portfolio companies".

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Do Temasek and GIC not seek to share ideas and experience with their investee companies in ways that may enhance long-term shareholder value?

sections.label: Temasek GIC role and Budget surplus
sections.summary: The Member asks if a hands-off approach is a lost opportunity, citing Santiago Principles 16 and 19, then notes Heng Swee Keat's announcement of a $9.6 billion FY2017 Budget surplus, over five times the $1.9 billion forecast.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If Temasek and GIC are totally hands off in this sense, would this not be a lost opportunity since they have the opportunity to share learnings where permissible across their portfolio companies and from their past experience as investors, not to mention connecting investees to agencies like the Economic Development Board (EDB) which can generate win-win opportunities for investees and Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Playing such a role, if kept within the boundaries of permissible information and idea dissemination, could be consistent with the Santiago Principle No 16 on operational independence while advancing Principle No 19 on commercial orientation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat's announcement on the $9.6 billion Budget surplus out of fiscal year 2017 is definitely a pleasant surprise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is more than five times the initial surplus forecast of $1.9 billion.

sections.label: Proposed savings subsidies SG Bonus ratio
sections.summary: The Member suggests adopting a 65:20:15 ratio for savings, subsidies and SG Bonus allocation, using a conservative 15% approach while keeping savings at 65%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Taking a conservative approach of 15% and still keeping a reasonable high savings of 65%, I suggest we adopt a 65:20:15 ratio for our savings, our subsidies and our SG Bonus allocation.

sections.label: Donations and tax deduction extension
sections.summary: The percentage of Singaporeans donating money rose from 55% in 2013 to 58% in 2016, and the Minister said the 250% tax deduction for qualifying donations will be extended three more years until 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Although the ranking has dropped for the past two years, the percentage of Singaporeans who donated money has increased from 55% in 2013 to 58% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is heartening to hear from the Minister that 250% tax deduction for qualifying donations will be extended for another three more years until 2021.

sections.label: Progressive tax deduction for donors
sections.summary: The Member proposes a progressive tax deduction starting at 200% and rising by 50% to a maximum 500%, to attract more and higher-value donations, and asks the Government to study its feasibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Tax deductions can begin at 200% and increase in quantum of 50% reaching a maximum rate of 500%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The suggested model will make donating large amounts more attractive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such, the objective is not only to encourage more donors to donate, it will encourage high net worth donors in our midst to donate even more which will benefit our charities and organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This, in turn, will mean that the organisations will have to develop new and better programmes to extend their reach to others who may be in need but have yet to be served.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: All in all, such a progressive deduction tax model will have a far-reaching effect that will benefit Singaporeans as a whole.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I truly hope that the Government can consider the suggested progressive tax deduction for donors and study on its feasibility for implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Currently, taxi hirers can use rental of vehicles and fuel as tax deductibles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can a similar approach be adopted for full-time private hire vehicle (PHV) hirers?

sections.label: Tax deduction for private hire hirers
sections.summary: The Member urges the Ministry to allow full-time private hire vehicle hirers to submit vehicle rental and fuel expenses for tax deduction, noting IRAS states private car expenses are not deductible under national car population policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the licence, they now no longer have to register a company but are affected by the tax deductible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to allow full-time PHV hirers to submit their vehicle rental and fuel expenses for tax deduction purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A search of the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) website's frequently asked questions (FAQ) segment provides answer to this query: "the expenses incurred on a private car by private hire car drivers are not tax deductible because of the national policy to restrict the car population".

sections.label: Explaining water price increase
sections.summary: The Government should explain simply the basis for raising water prices by 15% in 2017, with another hike in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government should attempt to explain this in a simple manner so that the public can appreciate the basis of raising water prices by 15% in 2017, with another hike scheduled for 2018.

sections.label: Lifetime upkeep and maintenance costs
sections.summary: Value includes lifetime upkeep cost, and keeping maintenance costs down means making maintenance easy to do.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Value is also about the cost of upkeep over the lifetime of the project.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We also have to look at how to keep maintenance costs down and that means making maintenance easy to do.

sections.label: High-rise littering and CCTV cameras
sections.summary: Litter lands on horizontal beams, and NEA found column and strut layout makes CCTV cameras to catch high-rise littering very difficult or impossible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The litter lands on horizontal beams, difficult to clear.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I asked the National Environment Agency (NEA) if there was something that could be done, NEA has been studying this for some time and they have found that the layout of the columns, the layout of the struts, make it very difficult if not impossible to put closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras to catch high-rise littering.

sections.label: Ease of maintenance in design
sections.summary: Prudent spending requires looking at lifetime maintenance and cleaning costs, so ease of maintenance must be a design criterion from the tender stage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: As part of prudent spending, we must look at the lifetime cost of maintenance and cleaning and upkeep of buildings and infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And as part of keeping lifetime maintenance costs down for infrastructure, ease of maintenance has to be part of the design criteria early on at the tender stage.

sections.label: Lifecycle cost approach for assets
sections.summary: For assets with long lifecycles of 25 to 30 years, it asks whether Ministries adopt a lifecycle cost approach covering maintenance and spare part replacements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Lastly, where assets have a long lifecycle, say 25 to 30 years, are the Ministries adopting a lifecycle cost-approach to take into account the cost of maintenance and replacements of spare parts?

sections.label: Local construction companies facing competition
sections.summary: Local construction companies face increasing competition from foreign-owned firms and difficulty winning Government tenders, with foreign firms bidding near breakeven or slight loss.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Today, I would like to highlight a feedback that local construction companies have been facing increasing competition from foreign-owned construction companies and have found it increasingly difficult to win tenders for Government contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of a local construction company told me that the foreign-owned construction companies are winning tenders at a level which is near breakeven or maybe even at a slight loss based on their cost estimates.

sections.label: Foreign construction companies joint ventures
sections.summary: A speaker suggests requiring foreign construction companies to tender jointly with local players so local firms build track records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We may need them for the construction of high-security facilities for which a foreign-owned construction company may not be suitable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But surely, there must be a way to require that foreign construction companies must tender for a project under a joint venture with a local player so that our local construction companies have the chance to build up their track record.

sections.label: NTP industry transformation update
sections.summary: A speaker asks the Minister for an update on NTP implementation and whether it has benefited the economy and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: During that Budget, NTP was also presented as an example of an "industry-level transformation".

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: It was then mentioned that the initiative will cost an estimated S$100 million, while it could bring about man-hour savings of about S$600 million to Singapore firms.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide an update on the implementation and whether it has benefited our economy and businesses with higher efficiency since its inception?

sections.label: Borrowing for major infrastructure projects
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance said recurrent needs are funded by taxation and borrowing is considered only prudently for bankable major infrastructure projects.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, this is what the Minister for Finance had explained in his Budget Statement that we fund recurrent needs through taxation and we will consider borrowing for major infrastructure projects.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But even as we look at borrowing, we will only do so prudently and on a selective basis.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We should borrow for the right projects ‒ those that are bankable and generate adequate future revenue streams to repay the borrowing.

sections.label: Development expenditure share of Budget
sections.summary: For FY2018, development expenditure is around 28% of the total Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For financial year (FY) 2018, the share of development expenditure of the total Budget is around 28%.

sections.label: PUB surpluses and water infrastructure
sections.summary: PUB transferred $1.3 billion of surpluses to capital reserves for FY2012 to FY2016, insufficient for $4 billion in FY2017 to FY2021 water infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For FY2012 to FY2016, PUB has transferred $1.3 billion of surpluses into its capital reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: However, this is still not sufficient to fully cover the $4 billion that PUB will be investing in additional water infrastructure between FY2017 and FY2021.

sections.label: Budget cap and block budget reductions
sections.summary: A 2% reduction to the budget cap and reduced block budget growth will further encourage fiscal discipline among Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The 2% reduction to the budget cap announced at the last Budget, and the reduction to the annual growth of the block budgets announced recently by the Minister for Finance will further encourage fiscal discipline among Government agencies.

sections.label: Gateway Process for infrastructure
sections.summary: Large infrastructure projects go through the Gateway Process.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, for large infrastructure projects, we have the Gateway Process.

sections.label: MOF Value-for-Money reviews
sections.summary: MOF works with agencies on Value-for-Money reviews to assess whether programmes achieve intended outcomes cost-effectively.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Third, MOF works with agencies to conduct Value-for-Money reviews to assess if our programmes are achieving their intended outcomes in a cost-effective manner.

sections.label: Resource allocation and manpower framework
sections.summary: Ministries have processes to allocate resources and extract productivity dividends, plus a Manpower Management Framework to keep public sector manpower growth sustainable.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Ministries have processes in place to more effectively allocate resources within their budgets, and to extract productivity dividends from their departments and Statutory Boards.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We also have a Manpower Management Framework to keep public sector manpower growth at a sustainable rate, in line with the resident labour force growth.

sections.label: LTA 4-in-1 depot savings
sections.summary: LTA's 4-in-1 depot saved the Government $2 billion, with co-digestion of food waste and used water sludge generating more biogas.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Ministers for Finance and Transport have shared one example, which is the LTA's innovative 4-in-1 depot that saved the Government $2 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Within this integrated facility, the co-digestion of food waste from NEA's facility with the used water sludge from PUB’s facility generates more biogas and enhances energy production.

sections.label: Green Mark Platinum cost premium
sections.summary: Green Mark Platinum building projects incur a 3% to 5% cost premium, offset by downstream energy and water savings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: One example is when we do a building project to achieve the Green Mark Platinum standard, we, in fact, incur a cost premium of 3% to 5%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But the additional upfront costs are more than offset by downstream savings from reduced energy and water consumption.

sections.label: JTC pilot productivity estimate
sections.summary: After piloting on three properties, JTC estimates a 15% improvement in productivity and energy savings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: After piloting this approach on three of its properties, JTC estimates it can achieve a 15% improvement in productivity and energy savings.

sections.label: Parking app vehicle usage
sections.summary: Since its October launch, about 250,000 vehicles have used the app in over two million parking sessions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Since the app was launched in October last year, about 250,000 vehicles have used it on more than two million parking sessions.

sections.label: Library space per staff
sections.summary: Library space managed per library staff has more than doubled, from 88 sqm to 183 sqm today.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The library space managed per library staff has more than doubled from 88 square metres (sqm) per staff to 183 sqm today.

sections.label: Government procurements price and quality
sections.summary: About half of Government procurements today are not awarded to the lowest-priced bidder, being put out on a price and quality methodology.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: About half of all Government procurements today are not awarded to the lowest-priced bidder because they are put out on a price and quality methodology.

sections.label: Building projects quality weightage
sections.summary: For building projects, the weightage of quality has increased from a maximum of 40% to a maximum of 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For building projects, the weightage of quality has increased from a maximum of 40% to a maximum of 50%.

sections.label: Bulk contracts and Government spend
sections.summary: There are over 70 types of bulk contracts today, accounting for about one-third of Government spend in goods and services.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Today, there are over 70 types of bulk contracts, accounting for about one-third of Government spend in goods and services.

sections.label: Smaller construction contracts value
sections.summary: About four-fifths of construction contracts are below $650,000 in value, which smaller local firms without a track record can participate in.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: About four-fifths of all our construction contracts are below $650,000 in value, which smaller local firms without a track record can participate in.

sections.label: Surplus returned to Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage states the surplus is returned to Singaporeans through various means, including the SG Bonus, Rail Infrastructure Fund, and ElderShield subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And we have a whole series of programmes and schemes in place to do this, including the Industry Transformation Map (ITM) for the Built Environment sector, which we will discuss more in MND's COS.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I should say we should not look at the SG Bonus in isolation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, the entire surplus is given back to all Singaporeans in different ways, not just through the SG Bonus.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The $5 billion we set aside for the Rail Infrastructure Fund to build future MRT lines, this will benefit all MRT commuters.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Another $2 billion is for subsidies on ElderShield premiums and other related support when the ElderShield review is complete, and that will be happening soon.

sections.label: Budget transfers and spending
sections.summary: The passage states some spending is for future needs, current needs like ElderShield premiums, and direct transfers like SG Bonus, GST Voucher, U-Save and S&CC rebates.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Some will be for spending for future needs, some will be for spending for current needs like the ElderShield Premiums, and some will be through a direct transfer like the SG Bonus.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And if we look at the direct transfers, we should also recognise that, besides the SG Bonus itself, there are other social transfers in the Budget, like the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Voucher, the Utilities (U)-Save rebates and the service and conservancy charges (S&CC) rebates.

sections.label: B2B tier launch date
sections.summary: The B2B tier of NTP went live in December 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The B2B tier of NTP went live in December 2017.

sections.label: SMEs financial statements tax submissions
sections.summary: The passage states SMEs can prepare financial statements and tax submissions in one day instead of four, targeting 300 SMEs by September 2018 and over 1,500 in the next 12 months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: By adopting such solutions, SMEs can now prepare their financial statements and tax submissions in one day, as compared to an average of four days previously.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The association targets to benefit 300 SMEs by September 2018, and over 1,500 SMEs in the subsequent 12 months.

sections.label: Employers seamless tax filing
sections.summary: Sixty employers benefited from seamless tax filing in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Sixty employers have benefited from this seamless tax filing in 2017.

sections.label: Simplified annual return filing steps
sections.summary: The passage states information will be pre-filled and companies need six steps to file the annual return, down from 24 steps.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Under the simplified process, some of the information will be pre-filled and the companies will just need to go through six simple steps to file the annual return, down from the current 24 steps.

sections.label: IRAS company startup kit
sections.summary: IRAS is introducing a new company startup kit, piloted with around 3,700 startups due to file their first tax return this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To help them get it right from the start, IRAS is introducing a new company startup kit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: IRAS will pilot this with around 3,700 startups that are due to file their first tax return this year.

sections.label: GSTV mobile updates savings
sections.summary: Since 2017, about 790,000 GSTV recipients with SingPass-registered mobile numbers received updates, cutting physical letters and saving $300,000 and 160 trees annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Since 2017, about 790,000 GSTV recipients with mobile numbers registered with SingPass have benefited from timely and accessible updates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have cut down physical letters, saving $300,000 and 160 trees annually.

sections.label: Public sector late payment rate
sections.summary: The public sector's late payment rate has been reduced by more than half over three years and currently averages 6.5%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The late payment rate for the public sector, comprising both Ministries and Statutory Boards, has been reduced by more than half over the past three years and is currently at an average of 6.5%.

sections.label: Private hire car driver deductions
sections.summary: Private hire ride-hailing car drivers cannot claim tax deduction on car-related expenses but can claim non-car related expenses such as commissions and mobile phone costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Currently, private hire ride-hailing car drivers are not allowed to claim tax deduction on any car-related expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Private hire car drivers can, however, claim tax deduction on non-car related expenses, such as commission paid to third-party operators, administrative charges imposed by third-party operators, and the proportion of expenses for mobile phones used in the course of providing their services.

sections.label: Donations and tax deduction
sections.summary: Total individual and company donations rose 52% from $1.8 billion in 2009 to $2.7 billion in 2015, with Singapore's 250% tax deduction among the most generous.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Total donations by individuals and companies have increased by 52%, from $1.8 billion in 2009 to $2.7 billion in 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Internationally, our 250% tax deduction for qualifying donations is one of the most generous tax deduction schemes today.

sections.label: Reviewing policies relevance
sections.summary: The speaker said policies will be reviewed to ensure they remain relevant and effective.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As I said, we will review our policies to ensure that they remain relevant and effective.

sections.label: Ongoing design input process
sections.summary: Seeking inputs for design is ongoing to improve design for functionality and maintainability, not just aesthetics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Seeking inputs for design is an ongoing process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We already do that and we want to continue to do that to improve design, not just for aesthetics, like I have said, but for functionality and maintainability.

sections.label: URA connectivity requirements for developers
sections.summary: URA now requires private developers of new buildings to add connectivity linking buildings and last-mile connectivity within developments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: URA has required private developers now, for new buildings, to put in place more connectivity, linking up buildings to another, and then enabling some of the last-mile connectivity within the building development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It was not done previously, but we have stepped up our efforts to do this.

sections.label: MOF expectations of Temasek
sections.summary: As Temasek's shareholder, MOF does not get involved in commercial decisions but expects high integrity, governance and legality.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Essentially, as the shareholder of Temasek, we do not get involved in their commercial decisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But MOF's expectation of Temasek is that it must uphold the highest standards of integrity, highest standards of governance, do not get involved in anything illegal, and make sure that they adhere to the highest standards of corporate governance.

sections.label: Corruption as OB marker
sections.summary: Corruption has always been an OB marker, not just now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Actually, corruption has always been an OB marker, not just now.

sections.label: Borrowing figure and capital reserves
sections.summary: The speaker lacks the specific borrowing figure but reiterates that $1.3 billion was transferred into capital reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I would not have the specific figure of how much they would want to borrow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But all I would reiterate is that, as I have mentioned, they have transferred $1.3 billion into capital reserves.
